extracted.intended_audience: IMLS Museums for America (MFA) grantees/applicants and evaluation interviewers (project managers, staff, leadership, partners, community members)
extracted.subtask_description: Interview protocols and survey items used to evaluate Museums for America (MFA) grants, eliciting short- and long-term effects, sustainability, partnerships, organizational and community impacts, application experience, and evaluation practices. Includes the quantitative data tables and metrics used in the MFA program evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for not sustaining new audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: E1.4a What are the reasons you attribute to not sustaining these new audiences?

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative grant size compared to other grants
rubrics_metrics.description: E1.5 Was this MFA grant from IMLS larger, smaller, or about the same as other grants you may have received? (Larger / Smaller / About the same / No other grant(s) received)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess importance/scale of MFA grant relative to other funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of MFA grant funds
rubrics_metrics.description: E1.6 Were the MFA grant funds sufficient to complete the planned project activities? (No / Somewhat / Yes / Don't know)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures whether award amount met project needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term effects on the organization
rubrics_metrics.description: F1.1 Please describe any long-term effect(s) that the MFA project has had on your organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended probe to capture sustained organizational changes attributable to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term effects on community and community relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: F1.2 Please describe any long-term effect(s) that the MFA project has had on your community or community relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended probe for community-level or relationship outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpected long-term effects
rubrics_metrics.description: F1.3 Please describe any UNEXPECTED long-term effect(s) that the MFA project has had on your organization, community or community relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures unanticipated outcomes (positive or negative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project history and origination
rubrics_metrics.description: Background 1. Could you share with us the history of this project? How did the idea originate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes genesis and context for project decisions and design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience/community need targeted
rubrics_metrics.description: Background 2. What audience or community issue or need was the project designed to address?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines target problem or population the project intended to serve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with institutional mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Background 3. How does this project align with your institution’s mission?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses strategic fit and mission relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspects most successful and key success factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Implementation and Sustainability 1. Which aspects of the project were most successful? What factors do you see as key in the project’s success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies effective components and enabling conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation challenges and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Implementation and Sustainability 2. What challenges did your institution encounter in implementing the project? How did your institution meet those challenges?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects barriers and mitigation strategies/lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and practice of sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Implementation and Sustainability 3. What does sustainability mean to you in the context of this project? How have the project or component parts been supported since the grant period?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elicits respondents' operationalization of sustainability and concrete post-grant support mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key institutional learning and advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Implementation and Sustainability 4. What do you see as your institution’s key learning from this project? What would you advise another institution interested in a similar undertaking?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures transferable lessons and recommendations for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership involvement and partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnerships 1. Did the project involve partnering with other organizations? And if so, with whom did your organization form key partnerships?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents partner identities and roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of partnerships to institution and partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnerships 2. What was the value to your institution of partnerships developed through the project? To the partners?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses mutual benefits and contributions of partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and growth of partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnerships 3. Have these partnerships been maintained, and if so, how? What has grown out of them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for evidence of sustained collaboration and spin-off activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target/existing audience response and trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Effects 1. How did your target or existing audience respond to the program? What trends did you observe over time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects evidence of audience reception and longitudinal patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience continued involvement/growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Effects 2. How has the target audience’s involvement with your museum continued or grown as a result of the program?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures retention and deepening of engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in museum reputation/position in community
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Effects 3. How has this project changed your museum’s reputation or position in the community (beyond the target audience)? What indications of reputation changes have you observed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks indicators of broader reputational impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other community effects observed
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Effects 4. What other community effects have you observed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catches additional community-level outcomes not captured elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff capacity improvements and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational Effects 1. In what areas, if any, has the staff capacity improved? To what extent were these capacity changes the result of (a) new staff, (b) professional development, (c) strategic planning, (d) budgeting changes, or (e) new technologies? Could you explain how that built capacity?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes capacity building to specific mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: New internal relationships across departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational Effects 2. Did the project support new relationships within your institution, such as across departments? If so, who was affected? What forms did the new relationships take?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents organizational collaboration and structural change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in staff commitment to the organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational Effects 3. How did the project change staff commitment to the organization?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores morale, buy-in, and staff engagement effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes from organizational changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational Effects 4. What outcomes have occurred as a result of these organization changes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links internal changes to concrete outputs or results (e.g., new programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of formative evaluation in project shaping
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning and Evaluation 1. How did you use formative evaluation in shaping the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses role of formative evaluation in project adaptation/design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of impact evidence gathered and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning and Evaluation 2. What kinds of impact evidence did you gather (e.g., methods, approaches, participants, etc.)? What conclusions did you draw?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects methodological details of evaluation and resulting inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of evaluation findings for subsequent projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning and Evaluation 3. Have evaluation findings from this project been useful in designing or developing subsequent projects? Please explain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures learning and transfer from evaluation results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of outcomes-based planning/evaluation in later projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning and Evaluation 4. To what extent are you integrating outcomes-based planning and evaluation in subsequent projects? Can you give an example of how you have included it in subsequent projects?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses institutionalization of outcomes-driven practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project manager: reasons for applying and application history
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Manager Interview Application Process 1. Could you share with us the history of this project? How did the idea originate? 2. How did you decide to apply for the IMLS MFA funding? Did you apply more than once? If you applied more than once, did you get feedback and was it helpful?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures application motivations and usefulness of feedback in iterative applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project manager: comparison of application process
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Manager Interview Application Process 3. How would you characterize the application process compared with other grants you have applied for? How does it compare to other Federal grants you’ve applied for?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elicits perceptions of burden, rigor, or value relative to alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project manager: value and challenges of application
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Manager Interview Application Process 4-5. Did you find the application process valuable? If yes, what was most valuable about it? What was most challenging about completing the application?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies perceived benefits and barriers of the application experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project manager: cost-sharing approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Manager Interview Application Process 6. How did you approach the cost-sharing requirement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents financial planning and matching strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project staff: role and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Staff 1-2. Describe your involvement with this project. What was your role? How would you describe the implementation of this project? Did it go smoothly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes staff perspective on implementation fidelity and role clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project staff: new skills and application
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Staff 3. What new skills or knowledge did you gain from this project? How have you been able to use these skills or knowledge in subsequent projects?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures professional development outcomes and transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project staff: impact on work and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Staff 4-5. Did the grant have an impact in how you do your work? Are there any other ways in which the grant changed how you do your job, your responsibilities, or improved your ability to do your job?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses changes in job content and capacity resulting from grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project staff: involvement and views on evaluation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Staff 6. To what extent were you involved in evaluation aspects of the project? a. If you were involved in these, were the IMLS requirements valuable? b. What challenges did you face in meeting the evaluation requirements? How might these requirements better fit the needs of the MFA projects? c. What did you learn from the experience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gathers frontline staff perspectives on evaluation utility and burden and suggestions for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project staff: community feedback and sustained aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Staff 7-8. Are there other ways in which this grant affected your institution’s ability to serve the public? a. What kind of community feedback have you received about the project? 8. What other aspects of the project have been sustained since the grant period ended? Please describe. How were these projects supported after the grant period?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects evidence of public value and mechanisms for sustaining project elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum leadership: overall mission-level impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Museum Leadership Overall Impacts 1. Please describe the value of this grant for your institution in terms of your mission (e.g., offerings, audience, efficiency). a. How does this grant relate to what you consider your institution’s strength in serving the community? b. How does this grant relate to what you consider its greatest challenges?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level assessment of strategic contribution of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum leadership: project successes and challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Museum Leadership 2-3. What aspects of the project were most successful? What challenges did your institution encounter in implementing the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership view on success drivers and obstacles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum leadership: project impact on institutional activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Museum Leadership 4. How has this project impacted what your institution does? (with probes for conservation or outreach grants)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores practice changes in program areas relevant to grant type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum leadership: community impacts and engagement change
rubrics_metrics.description: Museum Leadership Community Impacts 5-7. Did this project change the museum’s reputation in the community? How has the community’s involvement with your museum continued or grown as a result of the program? Has the museum’s level of engagement with the community changed over time? If so, how? To what do you attribute that change?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership perspective on reputation and engagement trajectories and causal attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMLS grantee status and importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Museum Leadership IMLS Grantee 8-11. Are you regular applicants to IMLS or other federal funders? Was this the first IMLS grant your institution has received or one of many? How important was receipt of this funding for the institution? a. How did the size of the grant compare with other grants received? b. What kind of prestige is conveyed by receipt of the grant? c. Were you able to leverage the funds or the prestige in additional ways?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses funding history, symbolic value, leverage, and relative scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum leadership: effect of application/implementation on mission understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Museum Leadership 10-11. In what ways did the application process or the implementation of the grant impact how you understand your mission or how you understand how you can achieve it? How would you describe the value of the MFA program for an institution like yours?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines strategic learning prompted by application/implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum leadership: sustaining project and new opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Museum Leadership 12-13. What challenges have you faced in sustaining the project? What new opportunities for sustaining the project have emerged?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents barriers and prospects for continuation/scale-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum leadership: familiarity with outcomes-based planning/evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Museum Leadership Planning and Evaluation 14-16. To what extent were the outcomes-based planning and evaluation requirements familiar to your or your institution? Do you view planning and evaluation differently as a result of this project? To what extent are you integrating the outcomes-based planning and evaluation by IMLS in subsequent projects? Please describe current efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses awareness and institutional uptake of IMLS evaluation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community member: connection to grant and prior dealings
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Member 1-2. How were you connected to the IMLS MFA grant project (attended exhibit or program, community partner, volunteer or docent at the museum, etc.)? Have you had any dealings with the museum in the past? If yes, what types of activities or programs did you conduct with the museum?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterizes respondent’s relationship to museum and baseline involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community member: likes, learning, and community value
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Member 3-5. What did you like most about this project? What did you learn from your involvement in this project? What value did this project provide to the community?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures perceived benefits and learning outcomes from community perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community member: impact on impression and attendance/involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Member 6-7. Did the project have an impact on your impression of the museum? If yes, please describe. Did the project have an impact on your attendance at museum events or involvement in museum activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures behavioral and attitudinal shifts among community members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community member: museum-community relationship and other groups' participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Member 8-9. How would you characterize the relationship between the museum and the community? Do you know of other community groups that participate in programming with the museum? If so, what types of activities are they engaged in?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses networked participation and relationship quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community member: change in engagement over time and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Member 10. Has the museum’s level of engagement with the community changed over time? If so, how? To what do you attribute that change?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for perceived trends and causal factors from community perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner interview: institution's role and development involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner 1-3. What was your institution’s role in the MFA project? To what extent were you involved in developing the project? To what extent were you involved in the grant application process for this project? What was your interest in participating in this project? In what ways was this project valuable for your institution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures partner role, motives, and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner interview: partnership structure and evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner 4-6. How was the partnership structured? How has your relationship with the museum changed as a result of this project? Have you continued to work together as a result of the project? If no, why not? If yes, is this work on the same project or on a new project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents governance, continuation, and evolution of partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner interview: future partnerships and elements to continue/change
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner 7. Do you anticipate future partnerships with the museum? If so, what kinds of partnerships you would be interested in pursuing? What aspects of the partnership would you continue? Do differently?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elicits partner interest in sustained collaboration and areas for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner interview: network and community organization relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner 8-9. How would you characterize the relationship between the museum and community organizations such as yours? Do you know of other organizations that participate in programming with the museum? If so, what types of activities are they engaged in?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses broader partnership ecosystem and activity types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner interview: change in museum engagement over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner 10. Has the museum’s level of engagement with the community changed over time? If so, how? To what do you attribute that change?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner perception of engagement trends and causal attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey completion: contact and consent to include museum name in report
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion page requests number of people involved in filling out survey and asks if respondent would like a copy of the Executive Summary and whether they'd like their museum's name included in final report (Yes/No) and contact details (Name, Title, Organization, Address, Email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative consent and contact capture for follow-up and permission to identify museum in report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative evaluation metric: applicant/grantee status by museum discipline, region, and size
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables (e.g., Table II-1) report Applicants, Grantees, Non-Grantees counts and percentages by museum discipline group, region, and museum size with statistical significance indicated at p≤.05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate representation and award patterns across strata; chi-square tests mark significant differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative evaluation metric: applicants' operating budget statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Table II-2 Applicant Operating Budget: Count, Mean, Standard Deviation, Median, Minimum, Maximum reported for All Applicants / Non-Grantee / Grantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses relationship between operating budget and funding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative evaluation metric: museum discipline, size, and region distributions by year and other cross-tabs
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple tables (II-3 through II-14, III-1 etc.) provide cross-tabulations of discipline, region, size by number of applications, year of application, number and percent of awards, award rate by application attempt, grant category, primary activity area, and other dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the evaluative variables and cross-classifications used to analyze application/funding patterns and project activity areas; significance tests (p≤.05) flag notable differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative evaluation metric: application attempt and award rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables II-9, II-10 report Number and Award Rate by Application Attempt (First, Second, Third, Fourth) and by museum size with counts and percentages (e.g., funded vs not funded rates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures how persistence/attempt number and museum size relate to funding success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative evaluation metric: grant category and distribution over periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Table II-11 and following show counts and percent of applications by MFA Grant Category (2004–2007: Serving as Centers of Community Engagement, Supporting Lifelong Learning, Sustaining Cultural Heritage; 2008–2010: Building Institutional Capacity, Collections Stewardship, Engaging Communities) and their distribution by discipline, region, and size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines shifts in programmatic focus and who applies to which categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative evaluation metric: primary activity area of projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Table(s) III-1 list Primary Activity Area categories (Technology/Online Resources, Organizational Development, Programming, Exhibitions, Digitization/Collections) with counts and percentages by discipline, region, size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classifies funded projects by principal intended activity to analyze emphasis across the portfolio.
